results.name: medium-stp-off-baseline
results.title: Baseline · all bridges STP off
results.action: Reset the data bridge on all three CHRs over management SSH with protocol-mode=none (priority 0x1000 on both MLAG peers, 0x8000 on the access switch). Then run numbered 100 ms pings for 4 s in both VLAN 110 directions and both bypass directions, read back bridge, MLAG and LACP state, and send three ARP broadcasts each way. No fault is applied.

witness.name: dc1-access-switch1
witness.role: Dual-attached access switch and external RSTP root candidate

c1.name: dc1-traffic-host1
c1.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 1

c2.name: dc1-traffic-host2
c2.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 2

phases.name: Baseline
phases.expected: Both MLAG peers show mlag-state connected once ICCP is established, with CHR 1 as MLAG primary (lower mlag-priority) and CHR 2 as MLAG secondary. Every bond member of the MLAG bonds and of the access switch uplink is synchronized, collecting and distributing. With protocol-mode=none no bridge sends or forwards BPDUs, each ARP broadcast arrives exactly once, and all four streams deliver with zero loss.

results.title: One-way calibration · all bridges STP off
results.action: After the protocol-mode=none bridge reset and baseline gate, the runner adds a tc ingress filter on host 2's eth3 that drops bypass-forward echo requests (stream 301) for 2 s. It then removes the filter and observes 3 s of settling and a 3 s recovery window.

phases.name: One-way bypass cut

Stream 301 shows exactly one gap, with every request sent, and the gap's bounds enclose the measured 1.9–2.3 s filter interval. The reverse bypass and both VLAN 110 directions lose nothing.

results.name: medium-stp-off-reboot-secondary
results.title: MLAG secondary reboot · Medium lab, all bridges STP off
results.action: Resets all three bridges over management SSH with protocol-mode=none. It requires a loss-free probe baseline, zero BPDUs and one copy of each broadcast. It then reboots CHR 2 (MLAG secondary, mlag-priority=20) with `/system reboot`, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

witness.name: dc1-access-switch1
witness.role: Dual-attached access switch and external RSTP root candidate

c1.name: dc1-traffic-host1
c1.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 1

c2.name: dc1-traffic-host2
c2.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 2

phases.name: Secondary down
phases.expected: CHR 1 (MLAG primary) keeps the shared system ID, so the access switch's uplink bond and traffic host 2 keep their LACP partner and forward over their members to CHR 1. The virtual links keep carrier, so each partner drops its member to CHR 2 only at the LACP short timeout (3 × 1 s). With protocol-mode=none no port changes state and no BPDUs appear.

phases.name: Secondary back
phases.expected: CHR 2 keeps its bond members out of the 802.3ad bond until the MLAG system ID syncs with CHR 1 (mlag-init-delay), then adds them under the unchanged shared system ID. The access switch and traffic host 2 re-add the member to the same aggregator, so loss is brief or none.

results.name: medium-stp-off-reboot-primary
results.title: MLAG primary reboot · Medium lab, all bridges STP off
results.action: Resets all three bridges over management SSH with protocol-mode=none. It requires a loss-free probe baseline, zero BPDUs and one copy of each broadcast. It then reboots CHR 1 (MLAG primary, mlag-priority=10) with `/system reboot`, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

witness.name: dc1-access-switch1
witness.role: Dual-attached access switch and external RSTP root candidate

c1.name: dc1-traffic-host1
c1.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 1

c2.name: dc1-traffic-host2
c2.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 2

phases.name: Primary down
phases.expected: CHR 2 reverts its MLAG bonds to its own LACP system ID, so the access switch and traffic host 2 renegotiate LACP, with brief loss. The virtual links keep carrier, so they drop the member to CHR 1 only at the LACP short timeout (3 × 1 s). With protocol-mode=none no port changes state and no BPDUs appear.

phases.name: Primary back
phases.expected: CHR 1 keeps its bond members out of the bond until the MLAG system ID syncs (mlag-init-delay), rejoins as MLAG primary and restores the shared system ID. The access switch and traffic host 2 renegotiate LACP to the shared system ID, with brief loss.
